story: Gary stands at the bulletin board on Magnolia Loop in the hazy October heat, reading the Architectural Review notice tacked up beside his golf cart application. Donna is heading off toward the Rec Center with purpose in her step, while Hal is making his way out from his house to join the others on the street. Rosa is marching toward Town Square, all three of them clearly determined about whatever the day holds.
events: Gary (street bulletin board): Read the Architectural Review notice on my cart application
Hal headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: Rosa just read the Architectural Review notice on the bulletin board, and I'm standing right here with the sketches and clamp list. Everybody agreed to walk to the review desk together, and Rosa already read the notice, so I shouldn't ask again or repeat myself. The useful thing is to check the notice myself and see what it says about my cart application before we head over to Town Square. If it's still pending, I want every piece named at the desk, tuck-ons included, so there are no surprises on parade day.

parameters.content: Read the Architectural Review notice on my cart application

donna.thought_process: Rosa and Gary are both heading to the review desk about the cart, and I already said I'd go along. Gary just confirmed he's coming too, so no need to ask again. The sensible move is to actually walk with them. The review desk is probably at the rec center or town square, and the rec center connects to the courts, which is where I want Gary after. The rec center is the nearest connected zone, so I'll head there. Then maybe paddles after.

parameters.content: Walking over with Rosa and Gary to tell the review desk everything about the cart, then we're hitting the courts.

hal.thought_process: I've glassed the street twice already and the notebook is compiled for tomorrow's committee meeting. Sitting on the porch recounting the same flamingos won't add evidence. Gary's cart sketches bother me, and I told myself I'd see them with my own eyes before judging. A straight look from the street is the by-the-book thing to do, and it puts me on the Loop where I can speak to Gary and Donna face to face rather than only through binoculars. Besides, the Halloween decorations are going up, and I'd like to see whether anyone's pushing past the three-ornament limit.

parameters.content: Heading out to the Loop to get eyes on Gary's cart and the ornaments myself before the committee meets.

rosa.thought_process: Gary and Donna both said yes to walking over to the review desk together, so the asking is done. No need to repeat the invitation. The review desk is presumably at the Town Square, which connects from Magnolia Loop, and Gary has the clamp list and wiring sketches with him. I have the folder. Time to actually go, since the parade is Saturday and Thursday's review desk walk is the next step for our honest, tuck-on cart plan. Then the three of us can head to the courts after.

parameters.content: Walking to the review desk with Gary and Donna to lay out the cart plan honestly, tuck-on pieces and all.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
